example.detection_method: Implement advanced email filtering with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC enforcement to reject spoofed emails; use URL rewriting and sandboxing on URLs in emails; monitor web server logs for unusual POST requests containing credential submission; deploy network-based DNS monitoring for newly registered domains with homoglyph patterns; conduct phishing awareness training and simulate similar spear-phishing campaigns; enable multi-factor authentication to reduce impact of credential theft.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1110 - Brute Force (for credential validation post-harvesting)

validation.comments: The sample accurately represents a credential harvesting social engineering attack via spear-phishing email. The scenario description clearly aligns with the problem nature, describing impersonation of a trusted IT helpdesk and use of homoglyph domain to trick users. The technical data is comprehensive and realistic, including email headers, body, SMTP logs, phishing URL, domain registration details, web server logs, DNS lookups, and network captures, all consistent with a real-world phishing campaign. The indicators section effectively highlights key signs of the attack such as domain homoglyph, mismatched sender domain, neutral SPF, absence of DKIM, recent suspicious domain registration, unusual SMTP source IP, and DNS resolution to suspicious IPs. The detection methods are well aligned with the risk reduction strategies, covering email filtering, URL sandboxing, log monitoring, DNS monitoring, user training, and MFA. The inclusion of relevant MITRE ATT&CK techniques further supports the sample's completeness and correctness. Overall, the sample is detailed, plausible, and fully meets the validation criteria.
